cover.caption: Knirk, sa døra. Hvem er det som titter inn?
cover.alt: Jenta sitter ved rokken med en stor floke av lin i fanget. I døråpningen titter tre gamle koner inn: én med en kjempelang nese, én med store, rennende øyne og én med et kjempebredt, stripete skjørt.
cover.prompt: Night in the candlelit Little Chamber. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a huge, hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise. The door has creaked open, and three curious old faces peek in around it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking in first, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway. Rain streaks the window.

Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: Night in the candlelit Little Chamber. The Girl sits at the spinning wheel with a huge, hopeless tangle of pale-gold flax in her lap and looks up in surprise. The door has creaked open, and three curious old faces peek in around it, one above the other: the Long-Nosed Aunt at the top with her enormous nose poking in first, the Teary-Eyed Aunt in the middle dabbing her huge eyes, and the Broad-Hipped Aunt at the bottom, her wide striped skirt filling the doorway. Rain streaks the window.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Girl: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about sixteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and an enormous nose as long and thick as a cucumber, poking far out in front of her face with a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green shawl with a fringe, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and huge round eyes as big as saucers, pink-rimmed and always brimming with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously wide hips, so wide that her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.

Setting:
- the Little Chamber: A small, cosy room at the royal farm with honey-brown log walls and a low, beamed ceiling. A narrow wooden bed with a thick white duvet stands against one wall. A small table sits under a four-paned window with rain running down the glass, a wooden spinning wheel stands beside it, and a big upright wooden loom fills the far corner. A candle holder on the table, a striped rag rug on the floor and a plank door with an iron latch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. A poor hunter lives in a small log cabin deep in a spruce forest. The royal farm is a big, friendly cluster of honey-brown log buildings with grass roofs, carved gables and small-paned windows around a cobbled yard with a well. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a big wicker basket; spun, it becomes smooth, shiny golden yarn wound into soft balls; woven, it becomes a thick roll of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a neat pile of white linen shirts with shiny buttons. The Queen's servant girls are three young women in grey dresses, white aprons and white caps. The wedding is held in the royal farm's great hall, with six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long rainy spell at the end of summer: silver rain streaming down small-paned windows, dripping gardens in deep, wet greens and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sunshine sparkling on puddles and wet leaves. Indoors: warm candle and lamp light on flax-gold yarn, cream linen and soft wool colours. The wedding glows with candlelight, bowls of pink and white garden flowers and a tall cake. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. characters.name: Jenta
characters.description: En snill og modig jente som vil klare seg selv, men som også lærer at det er lov å ta imot hjelp.
characters.look: A slim, cheerful hunter's daughter of about sixteen with an oval face dusted all over with freckles, a snub nose, big hazel eyes, a wide smile and mousy-brown hair in one thick plait over her shoulder. She wears a plain pine-green linen dress with the sleeves rolled up, a short brown sheepskin vest, a leather belt and sturdy brown shoes, and has a blue jay feather tucked behind one ear.

characters.name: Bruden
characters.description: Jenta på bryllupsdagen sin, med blomsterkrans og brudekjole. Nå skjønner hun hvilken stor dag mostrene mente.
characters.look: The Girl on her wedding day: the same slim girl of about sixteen with an oval, freckled face, a snub nose, big hazel eyes and a wide smile, her mousy-brown hair now brushed out long and wavy over her shoulders under a wreath of pink and white roses and green myrtle. She wears a flowing cream-white linen wedding dress with lace at the square neckline and cuffs, a pale-green silk sash tied in a big bow, and the blue jay feather tucked into the wreath.

characters.name: Dronningen
characters.description: En håndarbeidsglad dronning som setter pris på det som er vakkert laget, og som til slutt viser omsorg og godhet.
characters.look: A tall, willowy, kindly queen of about fifty with a long neck, a long oval face, crinkly grey eyes, a slightly long nose and dark hair streaked with silver in a low, coiled knot under a small gold crown. She wears a sea-green gown with a frilled cream collar and a long rainbow-striped knitted shawl, and she is always knitting with two long wooden needles, a half-finished striped scarf and a ball of pink yarn.

characters.name: Prinsen
characters.description: En høflig og nysgjerrig prins som forstår at kjærlighet også handler om å ta vare på hverandre.
characters.look: A tall, slender, polite young prince of about nineteen with a long, clean-shaven face, a dimpled chin, a long nose with a little bump, earnest dark eyes under thick eyebrows and short, tidy black curls. He wears a small silver crown, a deep-teal velvet jacket with a row of silver buttons, a ruffled cream shirt, charcoal breeches and tall tan riding boots.

characters.name: Mosteren med den lange nesa
characters.description: Den første mosteren, som spinner alt linet for jenta om natta. Nesa har blitt så lang av all nikkingen ved rokken.

illustrations.anchor: Dronningen likte den nye jenta med en gang.
illustrations.caption: Dronningen likte den nye jenta med en gang. Det likte ikke tjenestejentene.
illustrations.alt: Dronningen strikker mens hun går over gårdsplassen, og smiler til jenta, som akkurat har kommet med en liten bylt. Ved brønnen står tre tjenestejenter og hvisker og surmuler.

Create one new illustration for a children's picture book, showing the moment described below.

Picture: Late in the evening in the Great Hall, the candles burning low. In front, the three aunts sit side by side at the long table, happily eating big slices of cake and resting at last: the Long-Nosed Aunt nibbles carefully around her enormous nose, the Broad-Hipped Aunt leans back on her two chairs with her eyes closed, and the Teary-Eyed Aunt smiles with a plate on her lap. Behind them, the Bride and the Prince sit hand in hand, and the Queen knits contentedly.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Long-Nosed Aunt: A small, slim, spry old woman of about eighty who holds herself upright, with a kindly, wrinkled face, merry little blue eyes, rosy cheeks and an enormous nose as long and thick as a cucumber, poking far out in front of her face with a round pink tip. Her white hair is in a small knot. She wears a long nut-brown dress and a big moss-green shawl with a fringe, and leans on a crooked walking stick.
- the Broad-Hipped Aunt: A short old woman of about eighty with narrow shoulders, a small round head and enormously wide hips, so wide that her skirt looks like a haystack. She has a square little face, a snub nose, bright squinting eyes, a gap-toothed grin and grey hair in a tight bun under a small round black felt hat. She wears a huge, bell-shaped skirt with wide red and ochre stripes, a white blouse and a short dark-brown knitted jacket.
- the Teary-Eyed Aunt: A round-shouldered old woman of about eighty, of middle height, with a soft, wrinkled face and huge round eyes as big as saucers, pink-rimmed and always brimming with tears, so she keeps dabbing them with a big white lace handkerchief. Her silver hair is braided and pinned in a ring on top of her head. She wears a dusty-rose dress with a white collar, a red tomato-shaped pincushion on her wrist and a silver thimble on one finger.
- the Bride: The Girl on her wedding day: the same slim girl of about sixteen with an oval, freckled face, a snub nose, big hazel eyes and a wide smile, her mousy-brown hair now brushed out long and wavy over her shoulders under a wreath of pink and white roses and green myrtle. She wears a flowing cream-white linen wedding dress with lace at the square neckline and cuffs, a pale-green silk sash tied in a big bow, and the blue jay feather tucked into the wreath.
- the Prince: A tall, slender, polite young prince of about nineteen with a long, clean-shaven face, a dimpled chin, a long nose with a little bump, earnest dark eyes under thick eyebrows and short, tidy black curls. He wears a small silver crown, a deep-teal velvet jacket with a row of silver buttons, a ruffled cream shirt, charcoal breeches and tall tan riding boots.
- the Queen: A tall, willowy, kindly queen of about fifty with a long neck, a long oval face, crinkly grey eyes, a slightly long nose and dark hair streaked with silver in a low, coiled knot under a small gold crown. She wears a sea-green gown with a frilled cream collar and a long rainbow-striped knitted shawl, and she is always knitting with two long wooden needles, a half-finished striped scarf and a ball of pink yarn.

Setting:
- the Great Hall: A long, warm hall of dark timber with a high ceiling and red-and-green rosemaling on the carved beams, lit by candles in iron chandeliers. Down the middle runs a long table covered with a white linen cloth and set with bowls of pink and white garden flowers, tall candles, plates and a tall, cream-covered cake, with carved wooden chairs along both sides. At one end stands a tall, carved double door.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. A poor hunter lives in a small log cabin deep in a spruce forest. The royal farm is a big, friendly cluster of honey-brown log buildings with grass roofs, carved gables and small-paned windows around a cobbled yard with a well. The flax is soft, pale-gold fibre in a big wicker basket; spun, it becomes smooth, shiny golden yarn wound into soft balls; woven, it becomes a thick roll of fine cream-white linen; sewn, it becomes a neat pile of white linen shirts with shiny buttons. The Queen's servant girls are three young women in grey dresses, white aprons and white caps. The wedding is held in the royal farm's great hall, with six guests in festive clothes.

This story's season, light and colours: A long rainy spell at the end of summer: silver rain streaming down small-paned windows, dripping gardens in deep, wet greens and soft grey-violet skies, then fresh, rain-washed mornings with sunshine sparkling on puddles and wet leaves. Indoors: warm candle and lamp light on flax-gold yarn, cream linen and soft wool colours. The wedding glows with candlelight, bowls of pink and white garden flowers and a tall cake. Accents: flax gold and the Queen's rainbow-striped knitting.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.
